data_as_of: Futures, VIX, DXY, oil, gold, BTC: Yahoo ~7:48–7:58 a.m. CT. Stock and ETF pre-market prices and volumes: StockAnalysis ~7:50–7:57 a.m. CT, cross-checked with Yahoo's screener (~7:48 a.m. CT). 10Y is Friday's close (Treasury cash market closed for Columbus Day).
headline: US futures are flat (Nasdaq-100 −0.2%) ahead of a week of bank earnings and Wednesday's CPI, with oil up ~2% after a Houthi strike on Riyadh's airport; CCC jumps 11% on buyout-talk reports and IREN rises 4% on a reported Anthropic cloud deal.
notes: Scheduled run at ~7:48 a.m. CT, before the 8:30 a.m. CT open: PRE-MARKET. Columbus Day: NYSE/Nasdaq open, US Treasury cash market closed (10Y shown is Friday's close). Japan closed (Sports Day). All movers use live pre-market data dated Oct 12 (StockAnalysis and Yahoo via the Mac browser).

Gap % = pre-market price vs Friday's close (StockAnalysis). Quality movers screened from Yahoo's US list ≥$5 and ≥$2B with an Oct 12 pre-market quote (~1,140 names across two screener passes), then confirmed on StockAnalysis. Names with <10K pre-market shares left out of the movers tables as too thinly traded: MIRM (+4.0%, 4.6K, Phase 3 EXPAND met primary endpoint), MANH (+4.1%, 2K), CWEN (+4.0%, 102 shares), STNG (+3.8%), BIIB (+3.5%, 21K kept out of top 10 by rank), CVLT (−4.4%), SQM (−4.3%), HRMY (−2.3%), SMTC (−2.3%), GDDY (−3.1%).
Benzinga's health-care list showed MIRM +13.4% at $97.52; StockAnalysis and Yahoo showed ~+4% at ~$89.4 on 4.6K shares — the Benzinga print was not confirmed and is not used.
Relative volume = pre-market volume / 3-month average full-day volume (Yahoo), so values are naturally small before the open.
Most-active list: StockAnalysis pre-market volume across ~140 high-volume and moving names — not an exhaustive scan. Dollar volume = pre-market price × pre-market volume from the same set.

Gap watchlist: ONDS (+4.6%, 3.2M) excluded — today's news is a product announcement (Regna AI with Palantir), not a listed catalyst type. SNAP (+3.5%, 1.8M) excluded — no company-specific news found. CCC and IREN catalysts are media reports (Bloomberg, The Information), not company confirmations; noted in risk.

Oil direction differs by source: Yahoo CL=F +2.1% ($93.76) and Brent +1.9% ($106.72) at ~7:48 a.m. CT; some overnight reports (Gulf News, HDFC Sky) had crude lower earlier after Trump's Russia-Ukraine energy-ceasefire announcement. Live Yahoo futures used.

Earnings: Yahoo's US earnings calendar shows none for today; Nasdaq lists only micro-caps NCPL, RMCF and MSS (time not supplied). CNBC movers page blocked (Access Denied) in both WebFetch and the Mac browser; Yahoo, 24/7 Wall St, Daily Trade Alert, Stocktwits and Benzinga used instead. WebFetch of api.nasdaq.com was refused for permission reasons, so the Mac browser was used.

Under-$5 lists are StockAnalysis top-20 pre-market gainers/losers (~7:57 a.m. CT) filtered to ≥100K shares and <$5; market cap = Yahoo shares outstanding × pre-market price; float not available. GIXI (+55%, $6.02, ~$15M cap) and TRAX (+25.8%, $40.05, ~$1.4B cap) fit neither table. CTNM (−25.3%, $9.99, ~$330M cap) likewise.

Leveraged ETF volume is pre-market volume as a share of a 3-month average day (30-day average not available). NYSE FANG+ has no pre-market quote (underlying_pct null). Proxies: NQ for Nasdaq-100, ES for S&P 500, RTY for Russell 2000, SOXX for semis, XBI for biotech (thin).
drivers: Futures are flat to slightly lower (S&P +0.0%, Nasdaq-100 −0.2%) after Friday's broad gains, as investors wait for third-quarter earnings — JPMorgan, Goldman, Citi and Wells Fargo report Tuesday, BofA and Morgan Stanley Wednesday, plus TSMC and ASML later in the week — and September CPI on Wednesday (consensus +0.6% m/m, 3.7% y/y headline; core 2.5% y/y). Oil is up about 2% (WTI ~$93.8, Brent ~$106.7) after a weekend Houthi strike on Riyadh's international airport kept Middle East supply risk in focus, partly offset by Trump's announcement that Russia and Ukraine agreed to stop attacking each other's energy infrastructure; tanker stocks (DHT, TORM, Frontline) are up 4%. The Treasury cash market is closed for Columbus Day, with the 10-year at 5.24% from Friday; Europe is up ~0.6–0.8% and Japan is closed. Chips are soft — Micron −2% and SK hynix −2% after China's CXMT reported progress on a next-generation DRAM design — while software gets analyst help: BofA double-upgraded Salesforce to Buy (+3.9%), but Wells Fargo cut Adobe to Underweight (−4.0%). Company news: Bloomberg reported GTCR and Elliott are in advanced talks to buy CCC Intelligent Solutions (+11%), The Information reported a multiyear Anthropic cloud deal with IREN (+3.8%), Bristol Myers reported two Phase 3 wins (+3.2%), and IonQ agreed to buy Elisity for up to $1.3 billion (−2.6%). Cleveland Fed's Hammack speaks at 11:10 a.m. CT.
